findings.text: MMIO interrupt cause uses the least significant position for virtqueue activity under VIRTIO_MMIO_INT_VRING and the next position for configuration change under VIRTIO_MMIO_INT_CONFIG.

Low network feature selectors assign VIRTIO_NET_F_CSUM to 0 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_CSUM to 1 and VIRTIO_NET_F_CTRL_GUEST_OFFLOADS to 2 and VIRTIO_NET_F_MTU to 3 and VIRTIO_NET_F_MAC to 5 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GSO to 6 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_TSO4 to 7 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_TSO6 to 8 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_ECN to 9 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_UFO to 10 and VIRTIO_NET_F_HOST_TSO4 to 11 and VIRTIO_NET_F_HOST_TSO6 to 12 and VIRTIO_NET_F_HOST_ECN to 13 and VIRTIO_NET_F_HOST_UFO to 14 and VIRTIO_NET_F_MRG_RXBUF to 15 and VIRTIO_NET_F_STATUS to 16 and VIRTIO_NET_F_CTRL_VQ to 17 and VIRTIO_NET_F_CTRL_RX to 18 and VIRTIO_NET_F_CTRL_VLAN to 19 and VIRTIO_NET_F_CTRL_RX_EXTRA to 20 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_ANNOUNCE to 21 and VIRTIO_NET_F_MQ to 22 and VIRTIO_NET_F_CTRL_MAC_ADDR to 23.

High network feature selectors assign VIRTIO_NET_F_DEVICE_STATS to 50 and VIRTIO_NET_F_VQ_NOTF_COAL to 52 and VIRTIO_NET_F_NOTF_COAL to 53 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_USO4 to 54 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_USO6 to 55 and VIRTIO_NET_F_HOST_USO to 56 and VIRTIO_NET_F_HASH_REPORT to 57 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_HDRLEN to 59 and VIRTIO_NET_F_RSS to 60 and VIRTIO_NET_F_RSC_EXT to 61 and VIRTIO_NET_F_STANDBY to 62 and VIRTIO_NET_F_SPEED_DUPLEX to 63 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_UDP_TUNNEL_GSO to 65 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_UDP_TUNNEL_GSO_CSUM to 66 and VIRTIO_NET_F_HOST_UDP_TUNNEL_GSO to 67 and VIRTIO_NET_F_HOST_UDP_TUNNEL_GSO_CSUM to 68, with compatibility aliases VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_UDP_TUNNEL_GSO_MAPPED at 46 and VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_UDP_TUNNEL_GSO_CSUM_MAPPED at 47.
Link status reports VIRTIO_NET_S_LINK_UP with value 1 for link up and VIRTIO_NET_S_ANNOUNCE with value 2 for required announcement.

Steering hash selection uses one-hot masks where VIRTIO_NET_RSS_HASH_TYPE_IPv4 is bit 0 and TCPv4 is bit 1 and UDPv4 is bit 2 and IPv6 is bit 3 and TCPv6 is bit 4 and UDPv6 is bit 5 and IP extended is bit 6 and TCP extended is bit 7 and UDP extended is bit 8.

Packet header flags assign VIRTIO_NET_HDR_F_NEEDS_CSUM to 1 and VIRTIO_NET_HDR_F_DATA_VALID to 2 and VIRTIO_NET_HDR_F_RSC_INFO to 4 and VIRTIO_NET_HDR_F_UDP_TUNNEL_CSUM to 8, while segmentation kinds assign GSO_NONE to 0 and GSO_TCPV4 to 1 and GSO_UDP to 3 and GSO_TCPV6 to 4 and GSO_UDP_L4 to 5 with tunnel markers at hex 20 for IPv4 and hex 40 for IPv6 whose union means any UDP tunnel and with GSO_ECN at hex 80.

Hash report codes run from VIRTIO_NET_HASH_REPORT_NONE at 0 through IPV4 at 1 and TCPv4 at 2 and UDPv4 at 3 and IPv6 at 4 and TCPv6 at 5 and UDPv6 at 6 and IPv6 extended at 7 and TCPv6 extended at 8 and UDPv6 extended at 9 in numeric order.

Control addressing uses class VIRTIO_NET_CTRL_RX at 0 with promiscuous 0 and all-multicast 1 and all-unicast 2 and no-multicast 3 and no-unicast 4 and no-broadcast 5, plus MAC class at 1 with table set 0 and address set 1, VLAN class at 2 with add 0 and delete 1, announce class at 3 with ack 0, multiqueue class at 4, guest offload class at 5 with set 0, coalescing class at 6 with transmit set 0 and receive set 1 and per-queue set 2 and per-queue query 3, statistics class at 8 with query 0 and get 1, where reply VIRTIO_NET_OK is 0 and VIRTIO_NET_ERR is 1.

Queue-pair provisioning uses command VIRTIO_NET_CTRL_MQ_VQ_PAIRS_SET at 0 with minimum VIRTIO_NET_CTRL_MQ_VQ_PAIRS_MIN at 1 and maximum VIRTIO_NET_CTRL_MQ_VQ_PAIRS_MAX at hex 8000, plus VIRTIO_NET_CTRL_MQ_RSS_CONFIG at 1 and VIRTIO_NET_CTRL_MQ_HASH_CONFIG at 2.

Statistics capability mask places receive basic, checksum, segmentation and speed at bits 0 through 3 and transmit basic, checksum, segmentation and speed at bits 16 through 19 and control queue at bit 32, while reply headers use the matching small values 0 through 3 and 16 through 19 and 32.

Legacy PCI transport places host features at 0 and guest features at 4 and queue address at 8 and queue size at 12 and queue selector at 14 and queue notifier at 16 and device status at 18 and interrupt status at 19 and configuration vector at 20 and queue vector at 22, with interface version 0 and address shift 12 and ring alignment 4096 and configuration interrupt marker hex 2 and no-vector value hex FFFF, while the device configuration offset itself varies with MSI-X mode.

Modern PCI capability identities assign common configuration to 1 and notification area to 2 and interrupt status to 3 and device configuration to 4 and PCI configuration access to 5 and shared memory to 8 and vendor data to 9.

Device configuration virtio_net_config starts with a six-octet link address member, then a two-octet status member, then a two-octet queue-pair maximum member, then a two-octet MTU advice member, then a four-octet speed member in megabits, then a one-octet duplex member, then a one-octet RSS key size limit, then a two-octet RSS table length limit, then a four-octet supported hash mask, stored packed without padding.

Version one packet header virtio_net_hdr_v1 begins with one-octet flag and segmentation members, continues with two-octet header length and segment size members, then offers an overlapping area usable either as checksum start and offset or as coalescing segment and duplicate-acknowledgement counts, and finishes with a two-octet merged-buffer count.

Hash header virtio_net_hdr_v1_hash extends the version one header with a four-octet hash value split low then high plus a two-octet report kind plus two-octet padding, and tunnel header virtio_net_hdr_v1_hash_tunnel appends two further two-octet offsets for outer transport and inner network positions.

Legacy header virtio_net_hdr holds flag and segmentation octets plus header length plus segment size plus checksum start plus checksum offset, while merged variant virtio_net_hdr_mrg_rxbuf appends a merged-buffer count after that fixed prefix.

Control envelope virtio_net_ctrl_hdr is two octets naming class then command with one-octet acknowledgement, MAC update virtio_net_ctrl_mac carries a four-octet entry count followed by that many six-octet addresses, and queue provisioning virtio_net_ctrl_mq carries one two-octet pair count.

RSS installation virtio_net_rss_config sequences hash mask, table mask, fallback queue, variable steering table, transmit queue bound, key length and key bytes, with split forms virtio_net_rss_config_hdr for the table prefix and virtio_net_rss_config_trailer for the key suffix, while hash-only virtio_net_hash_config sequences hash mask, four reserved words, key length and key bytes.

Coalescing controls carry packet-count and microsecond-delay pairs, with virtio_net_ctrl_coal_tx and virtio_net_ctrl_coal_rx covering each direction and generic virtio_net_ctrl_coal plus virtio_net_ctrl_coal_vq adding queue index and reserved word for per-queue operation.

Statistics exchange uses virtio_net_stats_capabilities with one 64-bit capability word, selector virtio_net_ctrl_queue_stats with queue index plus padding plus one 64-bit type word, reply header virtio_net_stats_reply_hdr with type, reservation, queue index, reservation and size, followed by per-category payloads for control queue, receive and transmit basic, checksum, segmentation and rate-limit counters.

PCI capability virtio_pci_cap chains vendor, next, length, type, bar, identifier and padding plus offset and length words, extended by virtio_pci_cap64 with high offset and length words and by notify capability with a queue-stride multiplier, while virtio_pci_vndr_data replaces bar positioning with vendor identity and requires reads without side effects.

Configuration members are valid only under their negotiated features, namely address under MAC, status under status availability, pair maximum under multiqueue, MTU under MTU advice, speed and duplex under speed reporting, and RSS limits and hash mask under steering or hash reporting, with pair counts limited to 1 through hex 8000 and with duplex using 0 for half and 1 for full and any other value meaning unknown.

RSS table entries present equal table mask plus one and key bytes present equal key length, hash installation keeps four reserved words for prefix compatibility, unclassified traffic steers to the stated fallback queue, and transmit steering stays within the stated maximum transmit queue.

Wire structures use explicit little-endian multi-octet fields and several control, statistics and PCI capability layouts are packed, so implementations must not rely on host alignment, padding or native byte order.

Control payloads ending in caller-sized tails such as address arrays, steering tables, keys and queue selectors require validation of counts, masks and lengths against transport bounds, with reserved words treated as opaque.

A merged-buffer count above one means one packet spans several supplied buffers, and hash or tunnel suffixes change header length and inner or outer offsets, so parsing must first branch on negotiated merge, hash and tunnel features.
